[F013] Repo: DontPanic
Env: dev
Project: (none)

**Finding 1 (high, correctness — project shadowing of a global profile id crosses a global model onto the wrong vendor harness):** Fixed in `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/config/resolvers.py`. The root cause was `_dispatch_harness_for` resolving profile identity through `worker_profiles.load_profiles()` — the fully merged global→project table — for every model layer, so a project profile shadowing a global id (`honey → claude` over global `honey → codex`) made the global-paired model look vendor-compatible with the shadowed harness. Following the auditor's recommendation, I added `_profiles_from_layers(layer_suffix)`, which builds the profile table as visible from the model's own layer (that layer plus deeper layers only, nearer winning per id), and `resolve_model` now maps the expected-harness name through that layer-scoped table instead of the merged one; `_dispatch_harness_for` takes the table directly and no longer touches `load_profiles`. Red/green TDD: I first added the regression test `test_project_profile_shadowing_global_id_suppresses_global_model` in `test_f013_worker_profiles.py` reproducing the auditor's exact evidence case — it failed with `AssertionError: assert 'gpt-global' is None` before the fix. After the fix it passes: dispatch resolves `honey` → `claude` and `resolve_model(..., harness="claude")` returns `None` (model suppressed), while `harness="codex"` still returns `gpt-global` — the pairing survives for the ven

commands_run: PYTHONPATH=scripts PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -c '<auditor repro: global honey→codex + gpt-global, project honey→claude; assert resolved model is None>'
